title: A Beetle Has a Bomb Inside. Why Doesn't It Blow Up?
subject: bombardier beetle

scenes.text: This beetle carries a bomb in its body. Why doesn't it blow up?
It stores two chemicals in separate chambers, hydroquinone and hydrogen peroxide.
When attacked, it squeezes them into a chamber full of enzymes. The mix heats to nearly one hundred degrees Celsius.
It sprays that boiling, irritating liquid in pulses, hundreds of times a second.
And each blast builds pressure that snaps the entry valves shut, shielding the beetle's own organs.
So the beetle never blows itself up. Every explosion happens in a sealed room.

description:
This beetle carries a bomb in its body. Why doesn't it blow up?
A study in Science used X-ray video of living beetles and showed the spray comes in rapid pulses of about 100 degrees Celsius.
Which animal defense would you want?
